1.why: Tokens are bound to the issuing session id and a fixed accountBinding, and /api/verify-token rejects tokens whose sessionId doesn't match the caller's session — though with only a single hardcoded 'local-recovery-account' there is effectively one user.

2.why: A token issued in one session cannot be used in another because verify-token enforces token.sessionId === session.id, so the same code does not work for another user.

3.why: No session invalidation/rotation occurs in /api/set-password, so the recovery session persists after the reset, but there are no other authenticated login sessions in this demo to remain valid, making the statement only partially true.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, enforcing HTTPS, but no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned so 'latest TLS version' relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are cryptographically random and only stored as SHA-256 hashes, and passwords are bcrypt-hashed; however hashing is not encryption and no other user data is stored/encrypted.

6.why: There is no real email delivery; the 'mock delivery' returns the raw token and reset link in the JSON API response and prints it to the browser console/on-page Logs panel, which does not guard the secret.

7.why: Inputs are type/length checked (validShortString), tokens restricted to /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/, JSON body size capped, and passwords validated against a policy; no raw input is ever interpolated into HTML or queries.

8.why: The only redirect-like navigation is history.replaceState to location.pathname plus a whitelisted hash, and testLink is a relative same-origin path, with CSP form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: The HTML page is a static String.raw template with only server-generated nonce and CSRF substitutions; no user input is templated into markup and client updates use textContent.

10.why: Errors return generic messages via safeError with no stack traces, and there is no server-side logging of secrets — though the client-side Logs panel intentionally displays the test token in the browser.

11.why: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes and tokens only as SHA-256 hashes with no hardcoded secrets, except the demo MFA code '482913' which is hardcoded in the source.

12.why: account.passwordHash starts as an empty string and there is no login endpoint accepting default credentials, but the hardcoded static MFA code '482913' functions as a de facto default secret.

13.why: recordFailure/limitStatus lock each category after 5 failures for 5 minutes (and recovery requests after 3), though counters are stored per-session so an attacker can reset them by dropping the cookie.

14.why: /api/recovery-request always returns the identical 'If an eligible account exists…' message regardless of the contact value, and the UI explicitly states the response is the same either way.

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues, hashed, 10-minute TTL, single-use, and bound to the session/account — user-specificity is limited only because the demo has a single account.
